full_counterpart_description.description_long: In remarks reported in October 2024, Donald Trump described some political opponents as an “enemy from within” and said the National Guard or military could be used if there were problems on Election Day. He characterized the people he had in mind as “sick people” and “radical left lunatics.” PBS NewsHour reported the comments in the context of the presidential campaign. The language drew attention because it suggested using military resources against a domestic political threat, a role distinct from the armed forces' ordinary national-defense mission. The comments were campaign rhetoric; no formal order, operational plan or troop deployment was reported. It also does not establish that every Democrat, Republican, or independent who opposed Trump was included in the quoted phrase. Trump made a conditional statement ahead of the election, but did not announce a specific deployment. A threat to use force and a military order are different actions.
full_counterpart_description.description_medium: During an October 2024 interview, Trump described political opponents as an “enemy from within” and said the National Guard or military could be used to address disorder on Election Day. He named “radical left lunatics” and referred to “sick people.” The PBS report covered the remarks ahead of the election. The remarks drew concern because they invoked military force against political opponents, but no order or specific deployment plan was reported.
full_counterpart_description.description_short: Trump threatens use of military against ‘enemy from within'
